messages:
alex: CI red on linux-integ after I regenerated poetry.lock to pick up latest constraints. auth tests failing — looks like our token helper is getting a str where it expects bytes.

samir: thanks for the ping. do you have the failing stack? any obvious dep bump in the lock diff?

alex: lock diff shows PyJWT 1.7.1 -> 2.7.0, and a couple small bumps. stack snippet: 
```
File \"tests/test_auth.py\", line 42, in test_token
  token = sign_payload(payload)
TypeError: can only concatenate str (not \"bytes\") to str
```

jin: FYI PyJWT 2.x changed encode() to return str by default. 1.x returned bytes. that would explain the concat error.

maya: can you repro locally?

alex: yep: `tox -e py310-integration` reproduces. downgrading to `pyjwt==1.7.1` in a venv makes tests green.

ci-bot: <ci details> https://ci.internal/redwood/1234 (linux-integ job) :red_circle:

samir: hmm. short-term options: pin PyJWT back in constraints/lockfile, or make our sign_payload tolerant of str/bytes. which do we want for a rollback?

jin: I'd prefer code be tolerant, but pinning is fastest to get CI green while we prepare a proper fix.

alex: Agreed. I'll open a quick PR to pin PyJWT in pyproject constraints and add a follow-up to make sign_payload handle both.

maya: pinging @eng-infra to coordinate lock regen once the pin PR merges, so it doesn't get reverted. :+1:

samir: I'll run a quick bisect on the lock regen history to confirm the single bump: `git checkout $(old-lock-commit) && poetry lock && git diff --name-only` — will post results soon.

alex: added repro steps to the PR description and the failing test link. Also included a tiny snippet to patch sign_payload if we want the faster code-only route: 
```py
def sign_payload(payload):
    token = jwt.encode(payload, KEY, algorithm=ALGO)
    if isinstance(token, bytes):
        token = token.decode()
    return token
```

jin: that patch looks safe and low-risk. plus a test asserting type(token) is str would catch regressions.

eng-infra-bot: created task #5123: "Pin PyJWT to 1.7.1 and follow-up: make token API compatible" and assigned to @samir.

alex: thanks — I pushed a temporary branch with the pin. PR incoming now.

maya: once PR merges, I'll schedule a lock-regen and run the full integ matrix.

samir: will also add a note to the release playbook: "watch for PyJWT major bump affecting encode() return type" so we don't surprise infra next time.

alex: good call. tagging @security for visibility (no vuln, just API change).

maya: noted. thanks everyone, re-runs in ~10m after PR. :rocket:
